title: MAMI Use of the Methoxyflurane as pain-killer in the prehospital management of Acute Myocardial Infarction
official: MAMI Use of the Methoxyflurane as pain-killer in the prehospital management of Acute Myocardial Infarction
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate that methoxyflurane self-administered by the patient suffering chest pain related to an acute myocardial infarction is at least as efficient in achieving pain relief that morphine.

interventions.name: PENTHROX 99,9%, liquide pour inhalation par vapeur de 3 mL

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient age ≥ 18 years
2. Patient managed in pre-hospital setting for a ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) : Chest pain < 12 hours with moderate to severe pain (VAS > 6/10).
3. Patient managed in pre-hospital setting for a ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI):  STEMI on ECG according to 2017 ESC guidelines
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous analgesic treatment for this episode of chest pain
2. - Clinical evidence of cardiovascular instability (PAS <90 mm Hg)
3. Altered level of consciousness due to any cause, including head trauma, drug or alcohol use.
4. Clinically significant renal impairment.
5. History of signs of liver damage after use of methoxyflurane or after anesthesia with a halogenated hydrocarbon.
6. Severe hepatocellular insufficiency (with encephalopathy),,
7. Acute head trauma and intracranial hypertension in the absence of controlled ventilation,
8. Uncontrolled epilepsy
9. Treatment with buprenorphine, nalbuphine and pentazocine, naltrexone, nalmefene or sodium oxybate
10. Breastfeeding, in case of initiation or continuation after birth of a long-term treatment.
11. Malignant hyperthermia: known malignant hyperthermia or genetic predisposition of the patient.
12. Hypersensitivity to morphine, methoxyflurane, any fluorinated anesthetic or any of the excipients listed in SmPC
13. History of serious adverse effects of the patient or his family after administration of inhaled anesthetics.
14. Incapacity to self-assess pain intensity
15. Incapacity to methoxyflurane self-administration
16. Pregnancy, minors or incapacity (tutelle, curatelle)
17. Participation in another interventional study involving human participants or being in the exclusion period at the end of a previous study involving human participants
18. Absence of a Social Security
19. Clinical evidence of respiratory depression.
20. Decompensated respiratory failure (in the absence of artificial ventilation),
